text:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: elevated 5xx + p95/p99 latency spike observed on /v1/generate in eu-west-1. Alert: 3xx->5xx ratio > 5% over 5m, p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1800ms. Pager: @alex (on-call).

alex: ack oncall. looking now. which deploys rolled in last 15m?

maria: can confirm a deploy to serving-runtime:stable at 1789455600 pushed ~12m ago. Canary looked ok at first.

sam: i'm seeing tons of 504s from the edge->gateway within the same window, and kube pods on fleet-b pool have high request queues. small bursts of `worker stuck waiting for kv-cache` in logs.

toni: tagging metrics: p95 1.8s, p99 4.6s, error-rate 5xx ~ 7% across eu-west-1, traffic shaping not triggered. Customer impact: multiple orgs report degraded response and timeouts. CS ticket created: CS-4556.

alex: starting quick triage. hypothesis: recent runtime change to batching/continuous-batch-size default. If batcher blocks, p99 blow-up.

sam: running `kubectl logs --since=10m -l app=redwood-runtime -n serving | grep -i "kv-cache" | tail -n 100` — seeing repeated `KVCache: miss -> fetching prefix, lock held` and `batcher timeout expired` in same timestamps.

maria: also seeing redis times increase for prefix cache: latency spikes to 120ms for KEYS. Could be an infra blip + new batching sensitivity.

pj: can we toggle circuit-breaker / reduce max batch size to mitigate? That should reduce head-of-line blocking.

alex: agree. quick mitigation plan:
- toggle global circuit breaker to drop long-wait requests (circuit-breaker api)
- reduce runtime max batch size from 64 -> 16 via feature-flag
- roll back latest serving-runtime canary if immediate mitigation doesn't restore SLOs

sam: applying circuit-breaker rule now: `POST /admin/circuit-breaker -d '{"route": "/v1/generate","max_wait_ms":800,"fail_open":true}'` returning 200.

incident-bot: circuit-breaker change recorded by deploy-bot (run_id: dbc-1789456795). Change will propagate to all gateways in ~30s.

alex: lowering batch size flag: `ffctl set serving.batch.max_size 16 --env=eu-west-1` — applied. propagation logs show featureflag propagated to 12/12 nodes.

maria: metrics update: p95 dropped to 420ms within 90s, error-rate down to ~1.2%. p99 still at ~1.1s but trending down.

sam: still seeing a few 504 traces tied to older connections from clients to gateway. Gradually clearing.

pj: any customer-facing actions? CS-4556 updated: "We're investigating increased timeouts in EU, mitigation underway; ETA 30m". let's keep CS updated.

alex: rollback decision: if p95 doesn't stabilize under 300ms and 5xx < 0.5% in next 10m, we'll roll back the canary that modified batching kernel. Right now mitigations look effective; hold rollback unless regression returns.

maria: small regression detected on a small subset with long-context requests; some requests still hitting >2.5s. Could be KV-cache hot keys causing head-of-line. I'm kicking kv eviction policy change to TTL 30s for hot prefixes as a targeted tweak: `redis-cli EVAL ...` (applied to eu-west-1 cache cluster).

sam: logs show eviction runs happening; relevant pod metrics show request queues dropping.

incident-bot: note: alert auto-escalation suppressed due to manual mitigation in progress.

alex: confirm with observability: running a short load test against canary to validate no regressions. `hey -n 1000 -c 50 https://eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — monitoring p95/p99.

sam: load test results: p95 210ms, p99 560ms, 5xx 0.3%. That looks acceptable for rollback hold-off.

pj: CS updated with new note: "Mitigations applied; degradation decreasing. Next update in 20m or earlier if changed." :thumbsup:

toni: preparing handoff to next oncall in 40m. @alex can you prepare summary and known mitigations for handoff? include commands run and runbook steps.

alex: will do. summary draft:
- root cause: batcher + kv-cache contention after recent serving-runtime change -> head-of-line blocking
- mitigations performed: circuit-breaker enabled on /v1/generate, feature-flag reduced batch size 64->16, KV-cache eviction TTL lowered for hot prefixes
- current state: p95 ~ 220-420ms, p99 ~ 500-1100ms, 5xx ~ 0.3-1.2% (down from 7%)
- next steps: monitor 30m, consider rollback of canary rev r789 if p99 stays > 1s or 5xx > 0.5% sustained

maria: I'll follow up on targeted cache fixes and a small change to redis cluster pod sizing for eu-west-1; creating infra task INF-7892.

sam: leaving a pinned snippet for diagnostic commands in thread:
```
# check runtime queue depth
kubectl exec -it svc/runtime-metrics -n serving -- curl localhost:9090/queues

# tail offending logs
kubectl logs -l app=redwood-runtime -n serving --since=15m | grep -E "batcher|kv-cache|timeout"

# toggle circuit breaker
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.redwood.ai/circuit-breaker -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","max_wait_ms":800}'
```

pj: tl;dr for next oncall: mitigations working; watch p99 and 5xx in eu-west-1. If regressions reappear, rollback canary and notify CS and customers in affected orgs.

alex: handing off to @toni at 1789460500. i'll stay available for 20m after handoff. good job everyone.

toni: taking handoff. thanks all — I'll post a brief incident summary and start a postmortem stub once things fully settle. tagging for follow-up: @maria (cache), @sam (runtime), @pj (customer comms).
